Definition: from G303 and G1325; to hand over:--deliver.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears once: the soldiers who brought Paul to Caesarea delivered the epistle to the governor and presented Paul also before him. It is a handing over — the letter and the prisoner both delivered into Felix's hands, and Paul's case passing to the next court.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for handing over carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the chain of custody — Paul passed from soldiers to governor, and the gospel with him.
RelatedEvents: Paul Before Felix, Festus, and Agrippa
